title: Rotate Out the Rotated Logs
description: Compress app.log.1-7 into /var/log/app/archive/ while leaving the active app.log untouched.
scenario: The app's rotated logs (app.log.1 through app.log.7) are eating space in /var/log/app and this host has no logrotate config yet. Compress each rotated log with gzip, then move the .gz files into /var/log/app/archive/ (create the directory). The ACTIVE app.log must stay exactly where it is, uncompressed.
symptoms: /var/log/app holds the active app.log plus seven rotated logs
The rotated logs are uncompressed and waste space
The house convention: compressed logs live in /var/log/app/archive/
The active app.log must never be compressed or moved
mission: gzip the seven app.log.N files and move them into /var/log/app/archive/, leaving app.log untouched at /var/log/app/app.log.

hints.title: Match the rotated set precisely
hints.content: The glob `app.log.[0-9]` matches app.log.1-7 but NOT the active app.log — that precision is the whole game.

hints.title: gzip in place
hints.content: `gzip file` replaces the file with file.gz — no extra cleanup needed before the mv.

hints.title: Wildcard the move
hints.content: After gzip, `app.log.*.gz` matches exactly the seven archives; move them into the archive directory in one mv.

hints.title: Why the [0-9] matters
hints.content: `app.log.*` would ALSO match the active log — one careless glob and the live log is compressed mid-write.

acceptance_criteria.description: all 7 rotated logs are archived as .gz in archive/
no uncompressed rotated logs remain in /var/log/app
the active app.log is untouched in place
